q1_issues.issue: The sealed complement drops the sentence's entire assertion — the "fourth most common" and "eighth most common" rankings, the "in men" / "in women" restrictions, and the whole second conjunct — leaving only the unqualified claim that it is a cause of cancer, exactly the widening the no-silently-dropped-qualifier rule forbids.

P is also flattened to top level as if `show` were factive; `show` is on neither the factive nor the non-factive list, and a hedged evidential ("further estimates show") must not put its complement into the KB as fact.
Same top-level flattening of the sealed (Of sk_thing_1 cancer) argument link, which cannot project even for a definite referent.
With the complement sealed under Theme the holder must be Experiencer, not Agent ("the holder is Experiencer exactly when the complement seals").
(Member sk_estimate_1 further) predicates the descriptive modifier of the group symbol; a descriptive modifier on a plural distributes over the members rather than riding the group-as-object.

q2_gaps: a superlative / ordinal ranking restricted to a population ("the fourth most common cause of cancer IN MEN"): Ordinal / Most / AmongMost have no slot for the comparison population, and the AmongMost guidance ("a stated domain restriction stays on the entity as its own atoms") would misplace it as a property of the ranked entity
evidential clausal-complement verbs ("estimates show that P", "data indicate that P") appear on neither the factive nor the non-factive list, so whether P may be asserted at top level is unspecified
notes: The antecedentless "it" correctly takes a `thing` witness and "cause of cancer" correctly takes the nominalization's Of oblique; everything that makes the sentence informative is nonetheless absent.
